title: Estonian-inspired half-pi shawl
subtitle: A fingering-weight half-pi semicircle with nupps and nupp rows in the Estonian tradition.
excerpt: A fingering-weight semicircular shawl using the half-pi construction, with nupp bobbles at the intersection of lace diamonds inspired by the Estonian lace tradition. Wingspan approximately 160 cm, centre-back depth approximately 62 cm. About 380 g of fingering yarn. Nupps are worked only in the final two sections.
sourceNotes: Estonian lace (Haapsalu lace) tradition is documented in Nancy Bush, Knitted Lace of Estonia (2008). The nupp technique appears extensively in Estonian patterns; the specific lace diamond with nupps used here is based on a generic Estonian diamond structure documented in Bush's book. The half-pi construction is Elizabeth Zimmermann's invention (1971). The combination is original to this pattern.

knitting.gaugeText: 24 sts × 48 rows = 10 × 10 cm in stockinette on 3.75 mm needles, blocked.
knitting.gaugeInPatternStitch: 24 sts × 40 rows = 10 × 10 cm in Estonian lace on 3.75 mm needles, blocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: An Estonian lace technique for making a bobble: work (k1, yo) 4 or 5 times into the same stitch to create multiple loops, then on the following purl row purl all the loops together as one stitch. Nupps create dense circular bobbles at lace intersections.
Elizabeth Zimmermann's logarithmic semicircle formula: stitch count doubles on increase rows spaced at 3, 6, 9, 18, 27, ... plain rows.

content.text: A fingering-weight semicircular shawl using the
half-pi construction
, with plain garter in sections 1 to 3 and Estonian lace diamonds with
nupps
introduced in sections 4 and 5. Wingspan approximately 160 cm, depth approximately 62 cm.

Nupps are the distinguishing feature of Estonian lace: small dense bobbles at diamond intersections, worked by increasing to 5 loops on one stitch and purling them all together on the return row. This is rated ADVANCED for the nupp technique, which requires very loose tension on the RS increase row to allow the 5 loops to be purled together on the WS. Budget about 380 g (about 1,520 m / 1,660 yards) of fingering wool.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: About 380 g (1,520 m / 1,660 yards) of fingering-weight yarn

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, 100 cm or longer

items.name: Tapestry needle, scissors, blocking mat, pins

content.text: Gauge

24 stitches and 40 rows to 10 cm over Estonian lace on 3.75 mm needles, blocked. Nupp rows may run slightly tighter per 10 cm than non-nupp rows; the average across sections 4 and 5 should be close to the stated gauge.
Stitches used

items.name: nupp
items.qty: (k1, yo) × 4, k1 into same stitch = 9 loops; p9tog on the following WS row

content.text: Pattern
Sections 1 to 3: garter
Cast on 9 stitches. Work half-pi sections 1 to 3 in plain garter (3, 6, 9 plain rows between increase rows). After section 3 increase row: approximately 65 stitches.
Sections 4 and 5: Estonian lace with nupps

Section 4 (18 plain rows before increase row 4): Work Estonian lace diamond pattern across body stitches. The 10-stitch lace diamond repeat: k3, yo, ssk, k1, k2tog, yo, k2. Place nupps at the diamond crossing point on row 9 of every 10-row diamond repeat: k4, nupp, k5.
Section 5 (27 plain rows after increase row 5): Continue Estonian lace with nupps. After increase row 5, approximately 257 stitches span the full width. Continue until wingspan reaches 160 cm.

Nupp technique: on RS nupp row work (k1, yo) 4 times, k1 into the same stitch = 9 loops on the needle. Work all other stitches normally. On the following WS row, purl all 9 loops together as one stitch. Work the WS nupp stitches with a slightly larger needle if needed to ease the p9tog.
Bind off
Work Jeny's surprisingly stretchy bind-off.
Common faults

P9tog too tight to complete: the 9 nupp loops were worked at normal tension on the RS. The nupp RS row must be worked extremely loosely: use a needle 1 to 2 sizes larger for the (k1, yo) loops only, then switch back to the regular needle for non-nupp stitches.

Nupps not round and firm: the 9 loops were not all gathered tightly together during the p9tog. Pull each loop onto the right needle as it comes, making sure all 9 are on the needle before pulling the stitch through.
Blocking
Soak 20 minutes. Pin the straight edge and the curved lower edge to the full 160 cm wingspan. The nupp bobbles stand out from the fabric surface after blocking.
Care
Hand wash gently in cool water; the nupps are delicate and should not be agitated. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next

A full Haapsalu shawl uses nupps throughout all sections from the first few rows, creating a dense field of bobbles across the entire surface. Work a small swatch first to master p9tog before committing to the full piece.
